title.narrative: Seedbombs' - increased drought resilience through regreening in Somalia

description.narrative: Direct beneficiaries: 1,314 peoplePastoralists (60): The project will support pastoralists through the planned regeneration measures (NRM training, establishment of tree nurseries, dissemination of direct seed supply) and value chain activities .Landscape Regeneration Committees (40 LRCs members): The project will establish four LRCs (one LRC per protected area) with a total of 40 members in the two target districts. At least 40% of the members of the four newly established LRCs will be women.Key Galmudug State Ministries (8): The project will support 8 government officials from three key Galmudug State Government Ministries for the project, i.e. the Ministry of Agriculture, Crop Production and Forestry, the Ministry of Water and the Ministry of Environment, which have complementary mandates in landscape management including rangeland management.Community members (1,200 people):Community members in the four target areas will benefit from the landscape regeneration protected areas and will be reached through awareness raising events on rangeland and land regeneration. This group includes men (50%), women (50%) and children in the target areas with vulnerable socio-economic status.CPD staff (6) - The project will strengthen the technical capacities of partners on landscape regeneration, climate resilient value chains and the DNH approach to quality implementation of interventions.Indirect beneficiaries: 22,140 peopleOther members of the target communities: 22,140 vulnerable pastoralists and agro-pastoralists in the target area, including men, women, children and people with disabilities, will indirectly benefit from the impact of the project. This group includes former pastoralists and agro-pastoralists who are not directly affected by the project but who can adopt improved practices based on direct observation, as well as those whose grazing lands are adjacent to protected areas and to which they have access when they are opened for grazing.

Overall Objective: The livelihoods and resilience of vulnerable livestock farmers in Galmudug are strengthened.Project Objective: 1,314 people in the districts of Adado and Dhusamareb are using dryland-specific reforestation and sustainable land management methods and improving their livelihoods.

The project aims to strengthen the livelihoods and resilience of vulnerable pastoralists and agropastoralists in Galmudug through the establishment of landscape restoration areas, afforestation activities and reintroduction of key grass and tree species through innovative biochar-loaded 'seed bombs' as well as improved knowledge on key rural value chains.From the pilot project, guidelines for the scale out sustainable landscape-restorative and climate resilient value chains will be developed and shared widely to key stakeholders. The project will also support the implementing partner CPD to develop a strategy for a Somali 'seedbomb' social enterprise to promote landscape restoration interventions in Somalia.
